mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO YoY decrease > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and decrease in Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals a robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and UNRATE decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint behavior of HOUST and UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) during a recession signals further economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease during recession does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) and decrease in Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a misalignment in monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases and FEDFUNDS decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint behavior of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent market downturns.
